title: fix(codex): recover managed startup after Homebrew Node upgrades
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes managed Codex startup failing with `ENOENT` after Homebrew removes the Node executable used by a still-running Gateway.

## User Impact

New managed Codex JavaScript launches can recover through the same Homebrew formula's available stable executable. The running executable stays preferred while it exists, and recovery does not search `PATH`. No configuration or migration is required; restarting the Gateway after upgrading Node remains recommended.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed launcher used `process.execPath` directly even though command relays already use `resolveLaunchableNodePath`. Reuse that existing owner through the existing **private-local** `process-runtime` SDK entrypoint. Configured commands, native binaries, and exact-runtime workers retain their existing behavior. Host-owned Git settings now remain separate from configured environment overrides: the existing spawn-environment owner applies the prepared private value after filtering, and the shared-client key hashes it. Configured `clearEnv` is no longer rewritten. This private launch field is not accepted as a user configuration option.

Required consumer checks also exposed two bounded fixture defects. The ACPX retention fixture kept its final rejected lookup promise—and therefore its generation—on the fixture's own stack; returning from a helper before collection releases that root without changing GC passes or assertions. The native-shell fixture could read the operator's Git configuration after filtering out `HOME`; its synthetic command now disables global/system Git config while preserving the `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` assertions.

Supersedes #174379, thanks @TheRealUnknownSoldier. Release-note context: managed Codex startup recovers after a Homebrew Node keg is removed while the Gateway remains running.

## Evidence

- New real-child regression: **red on base** with `spawn .../Cellar/node/26.12.0/bin/node ENOENT`, **green with this change**. Verifies child arguments and environment with `PATH` cleared. Only process registration is mocked in this fast regression.
- Focused Node: **34 passed**, 56.19 s including preparation; new regression 122 ms. Focused pinned Bun: **24 passed**, 29.05 s; regression 51 ms.
- Live production-client smoke: real managed `@openai/codex` 0.162.1 launcher, real process registration and initialization, then `thread/loaded/list` succeeded both before and after removing the still-running owner's disposable Node executable. Independent copies of Node 26.12.0 simulate removal of a Homebrew keg; this is not an actual Homebrew/cross-version upgrade or authenticated model turn. The isolated Gateway reached readiness, but its agent-scoped probe lacked credential authority in empty state, so full Gateway-to-Codex proof is not claimed.
- ACPX retention fix: a heap snapshot identified stack → rejected promise → error → captured generation. Original fixture retained `lookup:16`; the repaired direct probe retained nothing in three runs. Actual parent suite: **15/15 Node and 15/15 Bun**. Native-shell fixture: **4/4 Node and 4/4 Bun**.
- Scoped source/test `tsgo`, type-aware lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, SDK import-boundary check, and Madge (**0 cycles**) passed. Fresh independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Full `check:changed` was replaced by scoped checks under the campaign's SQLite-inventory time-budget override. The separate package-wide typecheck was unqualified due to declaration/root-directory resolution failures and is not counted as passing.
- Production **+14/-19 (net −5)**, tests **+108/-17 (net +91)**, docs **+4/-3**. The environment repair removes the clear-list rewrite; the original runtime wiring adds two lines and removes a redundant four-line module synopsis.

**CI repair and current-head validation**

- [Prior precise-scan failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39702927619/job/119576168172): `openclaw-dangerous-host-env-override-pivots` flagged the existing `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` clear-list rewrite at `transport-stdio.ts:117`. The repair removes that rewrite; private prepared Git settings now pass through the existing spawn-environment owner after filtering and are included in the hashed client identity. The Node fallback still changes only the command.
- [Prior import-boundary failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39702927704/job/119576832288): the new test reached into core `src/test-helpers`. It now uses `withTempDir` from the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-env` surface.
- OpenGrep **1.30.2**, verified against the official release digest: changed-path scan **0 findings**. Its parser still warns on the pre-existing `using` statement in `run-attempt-connection.environment.test.ts`; production files parsed successfully. No rule, exclusion, or suppression changes.
- Full additional-boundary runner: **18 checks passed**, including the repaired extension-test import guard; its only local failure is the inherited core-test root budget (**726 Gateway / 749 infra**, advisory limit **720**). A clean physical worktree at `a8cb9d320a8a` reproduces the identical failure. The prior CI job reports those same counts as warnings; no limits or severity settings were changed.
- Current consumer validation: **399/399 Node and 399/399 pinned Bun**, across **33/33 files on each runtime** (290.83 s / 177.55 s wall including preparation). Includes real Codex fresh/cold-resumed shell execution, private Git settings/cache identity, and a real removed-Node launch with `NODE_PATH`/`LD_PRELOAD` injection attempts filtered out. Focused types/lint/format and a fresh independent review through P2 passed.

**Inherited audio-worker failure**

The audio comparison below was performed on head `a8cb9d320a8a`; the subsequent repair changes only Codex-owned launch plumbing and tests. The same two `keeps RTP and media delivery running during a blocked Gateway` cases (direct sink false/true) timed out in every run on both revisions. Counts below aggregate three independent whole-file runs; each run has two timeouts and three passes.

| Revision | Runs with matching timeouts | Timed-out cases | Passed cases | Individual timeout range |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Takeover branch | 3/3 | 6 | 9 | 30.006–30.009 s |
| Clean origin/main | 3/3 | 6 | 9 | 30.006–30.011 s |

These comparison runs used the unchanged `extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-peer-worker.test.ts`, Node, isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and the same dependency lockfile. The baseline was a clean detached worktree at `2b18fc8eb8705b67ec0037290002be25ac72ee3d`, with a separate dependency tree. No retries, increased timeouts, weaker assertions, or audio-source changes are included. The inherited failure is recorded rather than claimed fixed.

Exact comparison command, run three times in each checkout:

```sh
env HOME="$isolated_home" OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$isolated_state" \
  TMPDIR="$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)" OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-peer-worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```
